question: How many key variables are used in the World Happiness Report to explain happiness levels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Happiness Report identifies **6 key variables** to explain variations in happiness levels across countries.
 
• The six factors include: **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption.**
 
• These variables are derived from the **Gallup World Poll** data, which surveys residents of various countries on subjective well-being and social factors.
 
• The report evaluates happiness levels as a combination of these objective and subjective indicators, allowing cross-country comparisons.
 
• The annual World Happiness Report is published by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (UN SDSN).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita:** A measure of economic output per person, used to evaluate the wealth and standard of living in a country.
 
• **Social Support:** Reflects the availability of family, friends, or social systems to provide support during difficult times.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy:** Indicates the average number of years a person can expect to live in good health.
 
• **Freedom to Make Life Choices:** Measures individuals’ perceptions of their ability to make personal and professional decisions independently.
 
• **Generosity and Perceptions of Corruption:** Generosity assesses acts of giving, while corruption perceptions evaluate trust in public institutions and fairness of governance.
 
• The World Happiness Report was first published in **2012** and has become a key resource for policymakers worldwide, emphasizing the importance of well-being as an indicator of progress.
